name: Fleet Foxes
label: Sub Pop
lede: Robin Pecknold and Skyler Skjelset started a band in Kirkland, recorded a debut in a parents' basement and put five-part harmonies at the top of 2008's year-end lists. Then the drummer left to become Father John Misty, and Pecknold went back to college.

eras.title: A basement in Kirkland and a Myspace page
eras.text: Skjelset and Pecknold grew up on Dylan, Neil Young and Brian Wilson in a Seattle suburb. They had no label and no money, so they made the debut in a parents' basement and let Myspace handle the rest.

years.h: Robin Pecknold and Skyler Skjelset start a band in Kirkland
years.p: The Lake Washington High School friends bring in Casey Wescott, Nicholas Peterson and bassist Bryn Lumsden. Pecknold's father Greg had played in the 1960s Seattle soul band the Fathoms.
years.xp: Pecknold had toured the U.S. in 2005 playing bass in the Seattle band Dolour. Skjelset's mother Peggi raised him on Dylan and Hank Williams.

years.h: The Pineapples lose the name and become Fleet Foxes
years.p: A name clash with another local band ends the Pineapples. Robin Pecknold picks Fleet Foxes because it sounds to him like some weird English activity, like fox hunting.

years.big: "It was obvious he had talent coming out of his ass."
years.h: Phil Ek, fresh off Built to Spill, produces the first demo
years.p: That's [[Phil Ek|974863b2-1c82-4bb7-b23f-54ddf2713e88]] on Robin Pecknold. The demo, made with Ek, is sold as a self-released EP, and by year's end the Seattle Times is praising Pecknold's lyrics.
years.xp: Ek, whose credits include [[Built to Spill|3ac482b8-1494-4071-a0e9-f192f9d2c2b0]], had met Pecknold years earlier and helped shop the demo to labels.

years.h: Craig Curran takes over bass from Bryn Lumsden
years.p: Late in 2006 Curran takes over bass and harmonies, ahead of the basement sessions for the debut.

years.h: Guitar amps go inside tipis for a basement debut
years.p: With no label, Fleet Foxes pay for the album themselves, recording with Phil Ek in Robin Pecknold's parents' basement and at Casey Wescott's home.
years.xp:
It took a year. Pecknold called the sessions constant and exhausting, the band re-recorded the whole album at one point, and he was sick for some vocal takes. They finished in November 2007, with the last vocal overdubs the night before the final mix.

Pecknold wrote in a log cabin his grandfather built in Plain, Washington, and ran up credit card debt that touring later paid off.

years.h: Myspace does the label's job
years.p: Word of mouth alone pushes Fleet Foxes past a quarter-million plays in two months. Robin Pecknold later credits much of the rise to illegal file sharing.

eras.title: Album of the year, almost everywhere
eras.text: Fleet Foxes took Sub Pop over major-label money, put out an EP and an album two months apart, and finished 2008 on top of the Pitchfork, Uncut, Times and Billboard critics' lists. Pecknold had half hoped the record would flop.

years.h: Fleet Foxes turn down the majors and sign with Sub Pop
years.p: Bella Union will release them in the UK. On bass, Christian Wargo replaces Craig Curran.

years.h: A spring tour with Blitzen Trapper, then SXSW
years.p: The tour starts February 28. By the March SXSW set, the European press is paying attention.

years.h: Sun Giant is a CD for the merch table
years.p: Fleet Foxes say the EP isn't their full ambition, just something to sell on tour. Pitchfork later shares its album of the year between the EP and the LP.

years.h: Josh Tillman, solo act, takes over the drums
years.p: [[Josh Tillman|379fb100-063e-4472-b7c2-5bb9eda435ed]], with a string of solo records as J. Tillman, replaces Nicholas Peterson around the band's Sasquatch! festival set.

years.src: Wikipedia: Fleet Foxes (album) · Wikipedia: Fleet Foxes
years.h: A 1559 Bruegel for a cover, and a No. 83 debut
years.p: Pieter Bruegel the Elder's Netherlandish Proverbs wraps the album. It enters at No. 83 on 8,000 copies, then tops the CMJ radio chart on June 24.
years.xp:
Robin Pecknold liked how the painting looks bucolic until you notice all the strange things going on in it. "White Winter Hymnal," he has said, is about friends who abandoned him in high school.

Rolling Stone gave the album four stars out of five and Pitchfork a 9.0. The Guardian called it "a landmark in American music."

It later went platinum in both the U.S. and UK and was Bella Union's first gold record.

years.cap: Fleet Foxes at the Capitol Hill Block Party, Seattle, July 2008
years.h: Pitchfork, The Times and Billboard all pick Fleet Foxes for 2008
years.p: Uncut gives it the first Uncut Music Award. Robin Pecknold had hoped it would fail so he could move on.
years.xp: By year's end it had sold about 120,000 copies in North America and 200,000 in Europe, and it topped six of the 17 year-end lists Metacritic tracked. Pecknold's own verdict on all this: disbelief was the only sane reaction.

years.h: Saturday Night Live books Fleet Foxes
years.p: The band that cut its debut in a parents' basement plays as musical guest in January 2009, eight months after the album.

years.h: Fleet Foxes bin $60,000 of second-album sessions
years.p: Rehearsals for the second album, in a rented house outside Seattle, go nowhere. The band throws most of it out, and the money was their own.
years.xp: Josh Tillman's solo tours that winter slowed things further. By December Robin Pecknold was describing a less poppy, more groove-based record built around 12-string guitar, citing Roy Harper's Stormcock and Van Morrison's Astral Weeks.

eras.title: The second album, and the drummer who walked
eras.text: The second album cost Pecknold a five-year relationship and a year in four studios, and it gave Fleet Foxes their highest chart peak. Then the drummer left to become Father John Misty.

years.h: Morgan Henderson swaps the Blood Brothers for upright bass
years.p: The former [[The Blood Brothers|b847568f-cd75-44c7-b87b-4f38a5a9f661]] bassist also plays woodwinds, making Fleet Foxes a six-piece for Helplessness Blues.
years.xp: Sessions ran from January to December 2010 across Reciprocal Recording and Avast in Seattle, Bear Creek in Woodinville and Dreamland in West Hurley, New York. Robin Pecknold's girlfriend of five years left over the strain the album put on them; they tried again once she heard it, then split for good.

years.cap: Robin Pecknold tuning his 12-string at the Vogue Theatre, Vancouver
years.h: "Helplessness Blues" goes out as a free download
years.p: Fleet Foxes preview the second album by giving away its title track three months before the record comes out.

years.h: Helplessness Blues climbs to No. 4
years.p: Fleet Foxes' second album is their highest peak on the Billboard 200, after a year in four studios. The cover is by Seattle artist Toby Liebowitz, painted by Christopher Alderson.

years.h: Sean Pecknold films "The Shrine / An Argument"
years.p: Robin Pecknold's brother, the band's go-to director, makes the video for the album's eight-minute centerpiece.

years.src: Wikipedia: Father John Misty · Wikipedia: Fleet Foxes
years.h: Josh Tillman exits for Los Angeles and Father John Misty
years.p: That's Robin Pecknold on the last tour, in a 2020 Reddit AMA. Josh Tillman played his final show in Tokyo on January 20, 2012, then released Fear Fun as [[Father John Misty|172053e5-a7fb-4548-a64d-c53858b5e775]] on Sub Pop that May.
years.xp: In an October 2020 Reddit AMA, Robin Pecknold said Tillman had really quit after recording his drums, and that Sub Pop would only release Tillman's album if he waited a year to tour Helplessness Blues. Pecknold said that tour involved substance abuse, sabotaged shows, ill treatment and trash talk, while the band paid Tillman for songs he hadn't worked on.

years.h: Helplessness Blues is up for a Grammy
years.p: Fleet Foxes are nominated for Best Folk Album at the 54th Grammy Awards, weeks after Tillman's last show.

eras.title: A singer goes to college
eras.text: Fleet Foxes went quiet while Pecknold went to college in New York. Two cryptic posts in 2013 and a leaked iTunes screenshot in 2016 were all fans had.

years.h: Fleet Foxes post "Step one" and "Step two," then delete both
years.p: A photo of a laptop, microphone and guitar goes up captioned Step one. The next day a broken mandolin follows, captioned Step two.

years.cap: Robin Pecknold at Music Hall of Williamsburg, Brooklyn, January 2014
years.h: Robin Pecknold is at Columbia, studying English
years.p: He announces on Facebook that he has moved to New York for an undergraduate degree at Columbia's School of General Studies.
years.xp: He left in 2016 to tour with [[Joanna Newsom|cb69e1f1-bc76-4df5-93c9-cf97dd8a3b5c]] and, as of 2022, hadn't finished the degree.

years.h: Neal Morgan, drummer for Joanna Newsom, joins the new songs
years.p: On Instagram, Robin Pecknold says new songs are underway with Morgan, who also drums for [[Joanna Newsom|cb69e1f1-bc76-4df5-93c9-cf97dd8a3b5c]] and [[Bill Callahan|c309d914-93af-4b3f-8058-d79c75ea89da]]. The core is a five-piece now, with drummers brought in as needed.

years.h: A Christmas iTunes screenshot leaks an album called Ylajali
years.p: Robin Pecknold posts an iTunes queue with an unknown album and a Nonesuch logo. Fans trace the name to Knut Hamsun's novel Hunger.

eras.title: Six years on, Crack-Up
eras.text: Six years after the last album, Fleet Foxes returned on Nonesuch with a long, knotty record named for an F. Scott Fitzgerald essay, and a drummer from the Walkmen.

years.h: Crack-Up gets a name, a label and a nine-minute single
years.p: Fleet Foxes announce the third album on Nonesuch, with "Third of May / Ōdaigahara" as the first single.

years.cap: Fleet Foxes live at Big Cat, Osaka
years.h: Fleet Foxes play their first show in years, at the Wilma in Missoula
years.p: The set runs through nine new songs plus a Bee Gees cover, "In the Morning," with [[Matt Barrick|ebba7a50-23fc-412d-9451-a9ac183b31b7]] of [[The Walkmen|b7834ebd-64ae-46c3-a930-2d3a52ee743a]] on drums.

years.cap: Robin Pecknold at the Palace Theatre, St. Paul, September 30, 2017
years.h: Crack-Up takes its name from an F. Scott Fitzgerald essay
years.p: Recorded at Electric Lady and Sear Sound in New York, with three drummers and the brass quartet the Westerlies.
years.xp: It came out June 16, 2017, on Nonesuch, six years after Helplessness Blues. At the Wilma a month earlier, Fleet Foxes had already played nine of its songs.

years.h: Iceland's Graduale Nobili sing "Crack-Up" for Record Store Day
years.p: Fleet Foxes release a choral rearrangement of the title track, sung by the Icelandic women's choir.

eras.title: Shore, released on the equinox
eras.text: Pecknold made the fourth album nearly alone, through anxiety and a pandemic, and released it with a day's notice. Since then the band has run on solstices, equinoxes and solo acoustic nights.

years.h: Robin Pecknold drives to Lake Minnewaska to finish Shore
years.p: Stuck in Greenwich Village in lockdown, with the lyrics unfinished and his anxiety spiking, he takes day-long drives and writes his way out.
years.xp: Pecknold said the pandemic made the anxiety disappear and put the music's importance in perspective. To finish fast, he made the album without Skyler Skjelset, Casey Wescott, Christian Wargo or Morgan Henderson, working with engineer Beatriz Artola.

years.h: Shore lands at 9:31 a.m. ET on the autumn equinox
years.p: Announced a day ahead on Anti-, it arrives with a 55-minute Super 16mm film by Kersti Jan Werdal. "Sunblind" names dead heroes from Elliott Smith and David Berman to former Shins member [[Richard Swift|dd5f8909-245d-458b-833a-cd6b698399ce]].
years.xp:
Guests include Uwade Akhere, Tim Bernardes and Grizzly Bear's Christopher Bear and Daniel Rossen. Pecknold described the theme as life in the face of death.

Metacritic scored it 87 out of 100.

years.h: Robin Pecknold plays the solstice alone in a Brooklyn church
years.p: A Very Lonely Solstice is a solo livestream from St. Ann & the Holy Trinity Church, dedicated to Sam Jayne of [[Love as Laughter|8f5c6093-27ba-402d-b092-4157c93a4104]]. It comes out as a live album a year later.

years.h: Shore gets a Grammy nomination
years.p: It's up for Best Alternative Music Album at the 64th Grammys.

years.h: Boston Harbor gets an equinox show on Shore's birthday
years.p: Fleet Foxes play Leader Bank Pavilion for a livestream, released that December on YouTube as Live on Boston Harbor. Christopher Icasiano is now the drummer.

years.h: Robin Pecknold books four solo acoustic nights in the Northeast
years.p: Fleet Foxes songs, covers and rarities at performing arts centers in April 2026.
